title: Cashless Payment Methods Philippines Businesses Should Accept
summary: A practical guide for Philippine SMEs on which cashless payment methods to accept — from QR Ph and GCash to cards, BNPL, and cross-border wallets.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** Philippine SMEs should prioritise QR Ph, GCash, Maya, cards (Visa/Mastercard), and InstaPay as their core cashless stack — covering the majority of Filipino consumer payment preferences. HitPay supports all of these payment methods in the Philippines, plus cross-border wallets from Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia. with next business day payouts in PHP for domestic transactions.


The Philippines is one of Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing digital payments markets. According to the[World Bank financial inclusion](https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/financialinclusion) data, digital financial services have expanded rapidly across the archipelago — but consumer preferences vary significantly by channel, transaction size, and customer segment. For SMEs in Makati, BGC, Cebu, or Davao, accepting only one or two payment types means leaving a measurable share of sales on the table.


The[Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA)](https://psa.gov.ph/) reports that SMEs account for 99.5% of all business establishments in the country. For operators in this segment, the right payment mix directly affects conversion rates, cash flow timing, and customer satisfaction.


## What Are the Core Local Payment Methods Philippine SMEs Must Have?


Five payment methods form the baseline for any Philippine merchant:


**QR Ph** — The national QR payment standard mandated by the[Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas](https://www.bsp.gov.ph/) (BSP). Interoperable across banks and e-wallets, it works for both online and in-person payments. Charges confirm at T+1.


**GCash** — The dominant consumer e-wallet in the Philippines with tens of millions of registered users. Essential for retail, food service, and online sellers. Charges confirm at T+1.


**Maya** — The second major e-wallet, widely used and supported across online and brick-and-mortar channels. Charges confirm at T+1.


**Cards (Visa and Mastercard)** — Required for customers without e-wallets, corporate purchasers, and international buyers. Online card transactions confirm at T+7; in-person card transactions confirm at T+2. For a deeper look at card acceptance infrastructure, the guide on[credit card payment for small businesses in Southeast Asia](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/credit-card-payment) covers key considerations.


**InstaPay and PESONet** — Real-time (InstaPay) and batch (PESONet) bank transfer rails that let customers pay directly from their bank accounts. Both settle at T+1 and are essential for B2B transactions and higher-value purchases.


## Which Additional Payment Methods Add Meaningful Revenue?


Beyond the core five, several methods serve specific customer segments and use cases:


**UnionBank Online** — Direct bank transfer via UnionBank’s digital platform. Activates instantly and settles at T+1. Relevant for customers who bank with UnionBank and prefer direct transfers over e-wallets.


**ShopeePay** — Integrated into the Shopee ecosystem, making it particularly valuable for merchants who also sell on Shopee or target online shoppers. Settles at T+2 and supports recurring payments.


**GrabPay** — Trusted by Grab app users across the Philippines. Useful for food, retail, and delivery-adjacent businesses. Settles at T+1.


**BillEase** — Buy now, pay later (BNPL) option that lets customers split purchases into instalments. Activates instantly and settles at T+1. BNPL increases average order value, particularly for electronics, fashion, and services.


**SPayLater** — Shopee’s BNPL product, relevant for merchants targeting Shopee’s user base.


**Over-the-counter (Bayad, ECPay, Palawan)** — Allows customers without bank accounts or e-wallets to pay cash at retail payment centres nationwide. Settles at T+1. Critical for reaching unbanked and underbanked customers outside Metro Manila.


For SMEs selling subscriptions or memberships,[recurring billing for Philippines businesses](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/recurring-billing-ph) outlines how GCash and ShopeePay support automated charge cycles.


## How Do Cross-Border Payment Methods Work for Philippine Merchants?


Tourist-heavy locations — Intramuros in Manila, the BGC strip, Boracay retail zones, and Cebu’s Mactan Airport corridor — benefit from accepting payment apps that foreign visitors already have on their phones.

Note: PayNow is a cross-border method for Philippine merchants — it lets Singaporean customers pay using their home app. It is not a local Philippine payment method. Cross-border activations typically process within 3–5 business days after submission.


Domestic transactions settle next business day in PHP. Cross-border transactions settle at T+1 calendar day through HitPay.


## How Should a Philippine SME Structure Their Payment Stack?


A practical approach is to build in layers:


1.


**Activate QR Ph and GCash activates quickly (typically within 1–3 business days) and cover the broadest customer base.**


2.


**Add Maya and InstaPay** — captures bank-transfer-preferring customers and completes the e-wallet coverage.


3.


**Enable cards (Visa and Mastercard)** — required for corporate buyers and card-preferring customers; activates within 3–5 business days.


4.


**Layer in BNPL (BillEase, SPayLater)** — once the core stack is live, BNPL increases basket size for higher-ticket categories.


5.


**Enable over-the-counter options** — if the customer base includes unbanked consumers or regional buyers.


6.


**Add cross-border methods** — activate PromptPay, and DuitNow if the business location or product category attracts foreign customers.


HitPay supports all of the above under a single merchant account with no monthly fees and no setup fees — merchants pay only per transaction. Accounts are approved within 1–3 business days. For a comparison of how HitPay’s QR Ph acceptance stacks up against other gateways, see[accept QR Ph with no monthly fees: gateway comparison](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/accept-qrph-with-no-monthly-fees-gateway-comparison-2025) .


The practical takeaway: most Philippine SMEs need at least six payment methods to cover their full customer base — QR Ph, GCash, Maya, cards, InstaPay, and one BNPL option. Merchants with physical stores in tourist corridors should add at least two cross-border methods. Over-the-counter should be considered for any business serving customers outside Metro Manila.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Do Philippine merchants need to accept over-the-counter payments?


Over-the-counter payment acceptance (through networks like Bayad Center, ECPay, and Palawan Pawnshop) is not mandatory, but it is strategically important for merchants serving customers outside Metro Manila or in market segments with limited bank account or e-wallet access. Philippine Statistics Authority data shows a meaningful share of Filipino households remain outside the formal banking system. OTC rails bridge cash-dependent customers into digital order flows, allowing merchants to capture sales without handling physical cash. HitPay supports Bayad, ECPay, and Palawan as payment methods for Philippine merchants.


### What is the difference between InstaPay and PESONet for business payments?


InstaPay and PESONet are both interbank transfer rails governed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. InstaPay processes real-time transfers up to ₱50,000, making it suited to consumer purchases and same-day B2B payments. PESONet handles larger batch transfers, typically settling within the same banking day, and is better suited to higher-value transactions or bulk payroll-style disbursements. Both are available as payment methods through HitPay for Philippine merchants.


### HitPay vs PayMongo — which is better for a small business in the Philippines?


HitPay is generally better suited to Philippine SMEs that want zero monthly fees and the broadest payment method coverage, including cross-border e-wallet acceptance. PayMongo is a strong choice for merchants that specifically want a Philippine-native platform with a built-in no-code storefront and are comfortable paying ₱349 per month for those features. HitPay covers GCash, Maya, QR Ph, GrabPay, ShopeePay, BillEase, SPayLater, OTC methods, and cross-border wallets — all with no monthly fee, next business day payouts for domestic transactions, and approval in 1–3 business days.


### How do Philippine merchants accept payments from foreign tourists?


Philippine merchants can accept payments from international visitors using their home-country e-wallet apps through cross-border QR acceptance. HitPay supports PayNow (Singapore), PromptPay and TrueMoney (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), and KakaoPay/PayCo/LINE Pay (South Korea) for Philippine merchants. The customer pays in their home currency; the merchant receives settlement in PHP. Cross-border transactions settle at T+3 (except Korean wallets, which settle at T+1), distinct from next business day settlement for domestic transactions. Activation for cross-border methods takes 3–5 business days after submission.


### Is there a fee to set up cashless payment acceptance in the Philippines?


Setup fees vary by provider. HitPay charges no setup fee and no monthly fee — merchants pay only a per-transaction rate. PayMongo charges ₱349 per month for its Storefront plan. Pricing for card transactions differs by gateway; see hitpayapp.com/pricing for HitPay's current Philippines rates. All HitPay pricing is exclusive of applicable taxes.


### What is QR Ph and how does it work for merchants?


QR Ph is the national QR payment standard established by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. It allows customers to pay using any participating bank or e-wallet app — including GCash, Maya, BPI, BDO, and UnionBank — by scanning a single merchant QR code. Merchants generate one QR code and it accepts payment from all supported apps simultaneously. Domestic QR Ph transactions settle the next business day in PHP when processed through HitPay.


### What cashless payment methods should a Philippine business accept?


At minimum, Philippine businesses should accept QR Ph, GCash, Maya, and Visa/Mastercard cards to cover the majority of digital payment transactions. QR Ph is a single QR standard that accepts payment from any participating bank or e-wallet app. GCash and Maya are the two dominant e-wallets. Adding InstaPay and PESONet for bank transfers, BillEase or SPayLater for BNPL, and over-the-counter options (Bayad, ECPay, Palawan) covers nearly all Philippine payment scenarios across online and in-person channels.
